subject: Re: Upcoming launch - traffic uptick, quota exception and product clarifications
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@brightlane.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@brightlane.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLane pilot launch window + expected request spike (Sept 16-18)

Hi Vivek / Karthik,

Thanks again for the onboarding call yesterday. We confirmed an internal launch window for our new recommendations feature: Sept 16-18 (internal beta, org-wide roll).

Quick preflight so we can avoid surprises on day one: based on our traffic model, we expect a 6x increase in inference requests vs our current pilot baseline, with peak 5-minute QPS ~420 and average sustained QPS ~160 across the 48 hour window. Attached is our updated traffic estimate workbook (brightlane_launch_traffic_estimates_v2.xlsx).

Can Redwood provision a temporary quota uplift or an exception for that 72-hour period? We ideally need a hard cap that prevents throttling for the first 24 hours and then gradual smoothing. Also please confirm whether prefix/KV caching will work with our session setup (we rely on short-lived conversational contexts).

We'd like to finalize a mutual action plan by EOD Monday (Sept 7).

Appreciate the help — Samira

--
Samira Patel
Head of Product, Recommendations | BrightLane
(samira.patel@brightlane.com)
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@brightlane.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane pilot launch window + expected request spike (Sept 16-18)

Samira — thanks for the estimates and the workbook. I looked through the peak numbers quickly. High level response: we can support the uplift but need a short cross-functional runbook so ops/product can respond if tail latencies rise.

Action items I'm proposing:
- Karthik: can you validate whether current plan for Dedicated routing + fallback to hosted variants will give the 24-72h runway Samira asked for? If not, what minimum capacity delta do you need?
- Marissa: ops will need a temporary soft quota bump and a clear rollback plan; can you own the exception request to finance and include a cost estimate?
- Lauren: product question from Samira on KV/prefix caching — does the short-lived session model block our caching heuristics? If so, what will the expected per-token cost delta be?

Samira — we'll come back with a concrete capacity commitment and the exception paperwork by Monday EOD. One ask: can you confirm hour-by-hour peak distribution for Sept 16 (if available) so we can size the 5-minute QPS windows?

Best,
Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane pilot launch window + expected request spike (Sept 16-18)

All — I ran a quick simulation against our routing and autoscale model. Notes:

- Baseline: current pilot uses a single dedicated pool (d-c6g) with modest headroom. The 6x uplift puts sustained QPS outside current pool capacity.
- Short-term options: (A) Temporary Dedicated capacity add: +2 GPUs of similar class (fastest to provision under Dedicated) — would cover sustained average and reduce tail risk. (B) Host fallback: rely on hosted catalog variant with slightly higher per-token cost but auto-scale faster.

Tradeoffs: option A gives best latency predictability but requires reserved commit for the month unless we route through burst credits (ops can open an internal sponsorship). Option B is cheapest operationally but needs graceful fallback logic in the client to handle model variant differences.

Cache note (to Lauren): for session lengths <60s we get diminishing returns from prefix cache. BrightLane's "short-lived conversational contexts" description suggests caching will help only for repeated identical prefixes (which I don't expect here). KV caching still helps if they reuse context keys across calls.

I'll prepare exact GPU counts/cost delta for Marissa and a one-pager for Samira with the two options by Monday morning.

— Karthik
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane pilot launch window + expected request spike (Sept 16-18)

Quick update from ops/finance side:

- I filled the temporary exception form (redwood_temp_quota_exception_form.pdf) and flagged it for priority review. Finance needs a nominal estimate for the 72-hour uplift.
- Cost estimate (rough preliminary): Option A (Dedicated +2 GPUs x 3 days): ~$6.8k additional infra cost + one-time ops handling fee. Option B (host fallback auto-scale): ~$3.4k expected consumption delta but higher per-token unit cost (we'd absorb some margin for a pilot SOC).

Requesting product confirmation on cache behavior and any feature flags we should enable to minimize per-token spend (Lauren). Also: we need BrightLane to sign off on a short SLO exception that authorizes temporarily higher 95th latency for 6 hours on day one if autoscale is catching up. Samira — can you confirm that's acceptable?

I'll prepare a short mutual action plan doc once Karthik confirms capacity numbers.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@brightlane.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@brightlane.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming launch - traffic uptick, quota exception and product clarifications

Thanks team — this is helpful. BrightLane confirms the temporary SLO exception for the first 6–8 hours of Sept 16 as long as we have a documented rollback and a communications plan if errors exceed 2% sustained for 30 minutes. We prefer Dedicated capacity (Option A) for predictability; please send final numbers and a purchase/commit path.

Attachment: updated workbook now includes hour-by-hour expected peaks for Sept 16 (tab 'hourly-peaks').

Next steps (agreed):
- Karthik: final capacity delta and exact GPU request by EOD Thurs (Sept 10).
- Marissa: finalize exception request + cost and route to finance for sign-off by Sept 11.
- Vivek & Lauren: confirm caching/feature-flag guidance and provide a short client-side fallback snippet we can use if we need hosted fallback.

If we get those in time we can lock the uplift and get procurement started.

Best,
Samira
Head of Product, Recommendations | BrightLane
